function: Downlink multicast and uplink receive or transmit-receive beamforming and power control for analog over-the-air FL aggregation; optimization-designed, the FL model is the learned element (pp. 2-3, 8).
system: Multi-antenna BS (N=16-64) and K=10-20 single-antenna devices, no RIS; 2 GHz carrier, 10 MHz bandwidth, analog transmission (pp. 3, 9-11).
method: CNN trained by federated mini-batch SGD with analog over-the-air aggregation; beamformers by block coordinate descent with projected gradient descent, not learned (pp. 3-4, 8-10).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. complex Gaussian (Rayleigh) channels with path loss -161.3-35log10(d) dB and 8 dB shadowing (p. 9); MNIST for the FL task (p. 10).
test_conditions: Each setting of N, K and SNR is a separate FL run over communication rounds, tested on the MNIST test images; averaged over channel realizations (pp. 10-11).
baselines: RBF (random beamforming) and SDUBF (separate downlink-uplink design), both defined in the paper; ideal error-free FL as upper bound; no earlier published aggregation design (pp. 9-10).
metrics: Test accuracy of the global model versus communication round, with 90% confidence interval; CDF of downlink and uplink SNR (pp. 10-11).
complexity: O(NK) flops per beamforming gradient; PGD typically converges in 5 to 1500 iterations for N=16-64, K=10-20 (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "The channels of all devices are generated i.i.d." as CN(0, I) fading with the paper's own path-loss formula; no 3GPP model, dataset or measurement is named, only "typical 5G wireless specifications [38]".
q2_support: p. 10: "measure the test accuracy of the global model update" on the MNIST test set; each (N, K, SNR) setting is a separate FL run (pp. 10-11); no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 10: "RBF: Randomly generated downlink and uplink beamforming vectors"; SDUBF is defined by the paper (p. 9) and ideal FL is an error-free bound; no earlier published aggregation design is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "each beamforming gradient requires O(N K) flops", and PGD "typically takes 5 ∼ 1500 iterations" to converge.
q5_support: p. 10: "We adopt the MNIST dataset [39] for model training and testing", a public dataset of the learning task only; channels are simulated (p. 9); no code or data link is given.
notes: Passes no_learning only through the FL-over-the-air rule: the beamformers come from optimization (block coordinate descent with projected gradient descent, pp. 8-9) and the learned element is the CNN trained across the devices (p. 10). Area 7: the problem is beamforming and power for the analog over-the-air aggregation and the downlink broadcast; the BS has N antennas, so the system check does not exclude it (p. 3). SDUBF is the nearest thing to a published baseline, but Section V-C (p. 9) defines it inside the paper, so q3=0; reviewer to confirm. The PDF is the arXiv version 2502.02034v1, read as preprint.
